articles.title: RBI Raises Investment Limits for NRIs and OCIs in Indian Equities
articles.excerpt: The Reserve Bank of India will allow NRIs, OCIs and all overseas individuals to hold larger stakes in listed Indian companies without registering as foreign portfolio investors, in a broader push to attract diaspora capital.
articles.image_caption: Indian rupee currency notes. The RBI has announced a package of measures to attract overseas capital into Indian financial markets amid renewed pressure on the rupee.
articles.nri_angle: NRIs and OCIs can now invest significantly more in listed Indian companies without FPI registration, with further limit increases expected.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian-American Astronaut Anil Menon Arrives at International Space Station
articles.excerpt: NASA astronaut Anil Menon, the son of an Indian immigrant from Kerala, reached the ISS on July 14 aboard Russia's Soyuz MS-29 spacecraft for an eight-month research mission — his first spaceflight.
articles.image_caption: NASA astronaut Anil Menon in his official portrait photograph at Johnson Space Center. Menon launched to the International Space Station on July 14, 2026, aboard Soyuz MS-29 for his first spaceflight.
articles.nri_angle: Indian-American astronaut Anil Menon, the son of a Kerala immigrant, becomes one of the few astronauts of Indian descent to reach the ISS, representing the growing presence of Indian-Americans in high-profile STEM and government roles.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: 71 Percent of Indian Americans Disapprove of Trump, but Democrats Are Not Gaining Ground, Carnegie Survey Finds
articles.excerpt: The 2026 Indian American Attitudes Survey reveals a community caught between rising discrimination, weakening partisan loyalty, and a 40 percent emigration consideration rate — all while economic anxiety dominates political priorities.
articles.image_caption: More than 5.2 million Indian Americans make up one of the fastest-growing demographic groups in the United States. A Carnegie Endowment survey finds the community is increasingly unsettled by discrimination and political polarization.
articles.image_credit: Photo by Daniel Torobekov on Pexels
articles.nri_angle: The survey is the most comprehensive study of Indian American political attitudes, tracking 5.2 million people navigating discrimination, immigration limbo, and shifting party loyalties.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian PhD Couple Wins $200,000 Settlement Over 'Food Racism' at University of Colorado
articles.excerpt: Aditya Prakash and Urmi Bhattacheryya alleged systemic discrimination after a staff member objected to the smell of palak paneer being reheated in a shared microwave.
articles.image_caption: A traditional palak paneer dish served in a bowl. PhD students Aditya Prakash and Urmi Bhattacheryya alleged that reheating this common Indian spinach-and-cheese dish in a university microwave triggered years of discrimination.
articles.nri_angle: Indian PhD couple faced food-based discrimination at a US university, highlighting cultural policing experienced by diaspora communities.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Germany Overtakes Traditional Rivals as Indian Students Flock to Free Tuition and Fast-Track Residency
articles.excerpt: Indian enrollment in German universities has doubled in five years as U.S. visa crackdowns and Canadian rejection rates push students toward Europe's zero-tuition powerhouse.
articles.image_caption: University students study on a campus. Germany's record 420,000 international students include nearly 60,000 from India, a number that has doubled in five years.
articles.nri_angle: Indian student enrollment in Germany has doubled in five years as U.S. and Canadian visa policies push families to explore Europe's zero-tuition education system.

articles.title: Sitharaman Asks Banks to Intensify NRI Outreach as FCNR Deposit Scheme Targets $50 Billion
articles.excerpt: India's finance minister urged public sector banks to ramp up engagement with the diaspora as the RBI's special foreign currency deposit programme gains traction with $10 billion raised so far.
articles.image_caption: Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman at an official engagement in 2025. Sitharaman urged public sector banks to step up engagement with NRIs to boost foreign currency deposit inflows under the FCNR scheme.
articles.nri_angle: Directly targets NRIs: enhanced FCNR deposit rates and government push for diaspora investment in India.

articles.title: India Bars ISRO Scientists From Quitting as Brain Drain Threatens Gaganyaan and Key Space Missions
articles.excerpt: More than 100 scientists have left ISRO in recent months, many joining private space startups, prompting the government to strip centre directors of authority to approve resignations.
articles.image_caption: The Indian Space Research Organisation logo at the agency's headquarters. ISRO faces an unprecedented talent exodus as over 100 scientists have resigned in recent months to join private space startups.
articles.nri_angle: ISRO's brain drain to private sector mirrors the broader NRI talent mobility story, with Indian scientists and engineers increasingly choosing market-rate opportunities over government service.

articles.title: Vinod Khosla Buys Seattle Seahawks for Record $9.6 Billion, Biggest NFL Sale in History
articles.excerpt: The Indian-American venture capitalist and Sun Microsystems co-founder outbid rival groups to acquire the defending Super Bowl champions from the Paul G. Allen Estate.
articles.image_caption: Vinod Khosla speaks at SXSW in Austin, Texas in March 2024. The Indian-American billionaire has agreed to buy the Seattle Seahawks for a record $9.612 billion.
articles.nri_angle: Indian-origin billionaire Vinod Khosla becomes owner of an NFL franchise in the most expensive team sale in league history, with another Indian-origin bidder among finalists.

articles.title: Immigrants Founded 59 Percent Of America's Billion-Dollar Startups
articles.excerpt: A new NFAP analysis of 775 US unicorn companies finds immigrants founded or co-founded 455 of them, worth a collective $5 trillion. India leads all nations with 96 billion-dollar companies traced to Indian-born entrepreneurs.
articles.image_caption: A diverse group of professionals collaborating in a modern office setting. Immigrant founders have built 59% of America's billion-dollar startups, according to NFAP research.
articles.nri_angle: India leads all nations with 96 billion-dollar US startups founded by Indian-born entrepreneurs, with six Indian immigrants among the 15 who have built two or more unicorns.

articles.nri_angle: Wangchuk, who inspired the film 3 Idiots, has drawn global attention to India's exam reform movement. Diaspora communities have followed his fast closely.

articles.excerpt: Natya Darpan's 11th edition in New Brunswick featured Marathi, Hindi, English, and multilingual drama — a diaspora cultural event that refuses to be a nostalgia act.
articles.image_caption: A scene from an Indian theatrical performance (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: The festival represents a maturing Indian American cultural ecosystem that goes beyond Bollywood and classical dance to engage with contemporary issues through multilingual theatre — a form of diaspora identity-building that receives little mainstream attention.

articles.title: Eight Michelin Stars, One Grocery Aisle: How Indian Cuisine Conquered America's Supermarket Shelves
articles.excerpt: Gymkhana Fine Foods launches nationwide in Whole Foods with $8.5 million in backing, as a wave of Indian restaurant brands — from Farzi Café to Dishoom — bet that American home cooks are finally ready.
articles.image_caption: A spread of traditional Indian dishes (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Indian diaspora entrepreneurs and chefs are driving the mainstreaming of Indian cuisine in American retail and dining — a cultural and commercial milestone that reflects the community's growing economic influence and culinary confidence.

articles.title: One Hundred and Twenty Thousand Doctors, One Alliance: How Indian American Physicians Just Built a Healthcare Bridge Between Two Continents
articles.excerpt: The India–America Health Alliance, announced at the AAPI's annual convention in Tampa, aims to connect US-based Indian-origin specialists with underserved patients in India through telemedicine, AI-powered training, and a decade-long research partnership.
articles.image_caption: Nita Ambani at the Reliance Foundation Hospital in Mumbai
articles.nri_angle: Indian American physicians — the largest ethnic medical community in the US, treating every seventh patient in the country — are formalising a healthcare bridge to India. The alliance turns the diaspora's professional capital into direct medical access for underserved communities back home.

articles.title: India's Tricolour in Boston Harbour: The Three-Masted Barque That Sailed Into America's Birthday Party
articles.excerpt: INS Sudarshini, a 513-ton sail training ship on a ten-month transoceanic odyssey, docked at Boston Fish Pier for the Sail250 celebrations — and the public can walk aboard through July 15.
articles.image_caption: INS Sudarshini flying the Indian tricolour during the Sail250 Parade of Sails off the Virginia coast
articles.nri_angle: India's naval sailing vessel is docked in Boston through July 15, giving NRIs in New England a rare chance to walk the decks of an active Indian warship — a floating embassy of maritime heritage at America's 250th birthday.

articles.title: Thirty-Seven Defendants, Three Gangs, One Assassination: Inside the US Indictment That Finally Named Nijjar's Killers
articles.excerpt: Operation Hardball charges Lawrence Bishnoi with directing the 2023 murder of a Sikh leader from an Indian prison cell. India says it will cooperate. The diaspora is still counting the cost.
articles.image_caption: The Robert F. Kennedy Department of Justice Building in Washington, D.C., headquarters of the federal prosecutors who unsealed the Bishnoi indictment
articles.nri_angle: The Bishnoi gang systematically used high-profile killings to terrorize the Indian diaspora in North America, targeting religious, social, and political leaders. The indictment is the most significant legal action yet addressing transnational criminal threats to Sikh and Indian communities abroad.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: An Indian Grocery Store Burned Before It Opened. A Mosque Replica Set Ablaze on a Bonfire. Inside Northern Ireland's Summer of Hate.
articles.excerpt: Belfast's June riots left 27 people homeless and an Indian community shaken. A month later, the arsonists have moved on to bonfires — and the 10,000 Indians in Northern Ireland are still waiting for the institutions to catch up.
articles.image_caption: Belfast, Northern Ireland — where anti-immigrant riots in June 2026 shattered the Indian community's sense of safety (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Northern Ireland's Indian community — roughly 10,000 people, many of them doctors, shopkeepers, and IT professionals who chose Belfast for its affordability — found itself at the centre of anti-immigrant riots in June 2026. The violence, including the arson of an Indian grocery store, exposed the growing vulnerability of diaspora communities in the UK.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Eleven Thousand Years of India, One Museum in Washington: The Diaspora's Audacious Bid to Tell Its Own Story
articles.excerpt: An Atlanta-based educationist has spent eight years building a case for a $14 million heritage centre in the American capital. He has now asked the Indian Embassy for a building it bought thirteen years ago.
articles.image_caption: The Embassy of India in Washington, D.C., where organisers have proposed housing the heritage museum
articles.nri_angle: A first-of-its-kind museum aimed at helping younger Indian Americans connect with their civilisational heritage, built by and for the diaspora
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: One Hundred and Fifty Dancers, Seventeen Countries, Three Nights Under the Acropolis: Inside the World Festival of Indian Dance
articles.excerpt: The fourth edition of the UNESCO-endorsed classical Indian dance festival opens in Athens this week, with performers from the United States, Canada, Britain, Oman, South Africa, and a dozen other nations gathering at the foot of Western civilisation's most famous monument.
articles.image_caption: A Bharatanatyam dancer performing at the Khajuraho Dance Festival earlier in 2026
articles.nri_angle: Indian classical dance traditions carried and performed by diaspora communities across 17 countries, showcasing how NRIs preserve and project cultural heritage on a global stage
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Three Indian-Origin Leaders Tapped to Co-Lead Federal Reserve Policy Task Forces
articles.excerpt: Raghuram Rajan, Raj Chetty, and Xbox CEO Sarah Bond (born Asha Sharma) will co-chair three of the Fed's five review panels — an unprecedented concentration of diaspora talent at the heart of U.S. monetary policy.
articles.image_caption: Raghuram Rajan, former RBI Governor and IMF Chief Economist, will co-chair the Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet Policy review
articles.nri_angle: Three Indian-origin figures simultaneously co-leading Federal Reserve policy review panels — spanning economics, data science, and corporate leadership — signals the breadth of diaspora influence in U.S. economic policymaking.

articles.title: India-UK Trade Deal Goes Live on July 15 — What Changes for NRIs in Britain
articles.excerpt: The new trade pact eliminates dual social security contributions for Indian workers in the UK, saves them roughly 25 per cent of salary, and opens 1,800 annual mobility slots for chefs, yoga instructors, and classical musicians.
articles.image_caption: India's Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal and UK Trade Secretary Jonathan Reynolds at the signing of the India-UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement
articles.nri_angle: 75,000+ Indian professionals in Britain stand to save roughly 25 per cent of salary through the social security pact, while new mobility pathways and tariff reductions reshape the economic relationship between the diaspora's two largest host countries.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian American Congressman Ro Khanna Detained at Gunpoint by Israeli Settlers in West Bank
articles.excerpt: The Silicon Valley lawmaker — a potential 2028 presidential candidate and grandson of an Indian freedom fighter — says IDF soldiers sided with the armed settlers who held his group for 75 minutes.
articles.image_caption: Congressman Ro Khanna, who represents California's 17th congressional district in Silicon Valley
articles.nri_angle: Khanna is among the most prominent Indian Americans in U.S. politics, a potential 2028 presidential candidate whose family story — from a freedom fighter's household in Punjab to Silicon Valley — embodies the trajectory of the Indian diaspora.

articles.title: Shrey Parikh Wins Scripps Spelling Bee With Record-Setting Performance — 31 of Last 37 Champions Are Indian American
articles.excerpt: The fourteen-year-old from California spelled 32 words in 90 seconds, breaking the spell-off record and extending the Indian American community's remarkable quarter-century dominance of the competition.
articles.image_caption: The stage at the Scripps National Spelling Bee, where Indian American contestants have dominated for a quarter century
articles.nri_angle: Indian American children have won 31 of the last 37 Scripps National Spelling Bees, a dynasty fuelled by community networks, immigrant-family educational investment, and organisations like the North South Foundation.

articles.title: From Fremont to Parsippany: Indian-Origin Mayors Are Making History Across America
articles.excerpt: Raj Salwan and Pulkit Desai lead a growing wave of Indian Americans winning local elections, reflecting the community's deepening civic roots.
articles.image_caption: Raj Salwan, the first Indian American mayor of Fremont, California
articles.nri_angle: Indian Americans are translating decades of private-sector success into local political leadership, with first-generation immigrants winning mayoral races in diverse cities from California to New Jersey.

articles.title: Indian American Neurologist Wins Lifetime Achievement Award for Transforming Global Stroke Care
articles.excerpt: Dr. Dileep Yavagal, founder of Mission Thrombectomy active in over ninety countries, honoured for reshaping how the world treats the leading cause of disability.
articles.image_caption: Dr. Dileep Yavagal, based at the University of Miami, received a Lifetime Achievement Award for transforming global stroke care
articles.nri_angle: Yavagal's career traces the circuit of the Indian medical diaspora — training in India, research breakthroughs at American institutions, and a global initiative that channels those advances back to underserved communities worldwide, including in South Asia.

articles.title: Ninety Artists, Eleven Days, One Ruptured World: Inside Vancouver's Indian Summer Festival
articles.excerpt: The sixteenth edition of Canada's premier South Asian arts festival is using comedy, raga, plant bioelectricity, and a closing ceremony in the Punjabi Market to argue that gathering is resistance.
articles.image_caption: A Bharatanatyam dancer performs at an Indian dance festival
articles.nri_angle: The festival is one of North America's largest platforms for South Asian artistic expression in the diaspora — a space where second-generation identity, cross-cultural collaboration, and community building happen through art rather than politics.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Billionaire, the Doctor, and the Toss-Up: Vivek Ramaswamy's Ohio Governor Race Just Got Real
articles.excerpt: Cook Political Report shifts the Ohio race from 'Lean Republican' to a dead heat. Polls show Ramaswamy and Democrat Amy Acton locked at 47-47 in a state Trump won by eight points.
articles.image_caption: Vivek Ramaswamy at a campaign event
articles.nri_angle: Ramaswamy's candidacy represents a new threshold for Indian American political ambition — a first-generation Indian American competing at parity in a major swing-state governor race, while the community's relationship with his brand of politics remains deeply divided.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Six Months of America's Remittance Tax: The One Per Cent Levy That Rewired How the Diaspora Sends Money Home
articles.excerpt: What began as a five per cent scare in Congress ended up as a one per cent excise tax on certain transfers. Half a year into enforcement, the real effects are subtler — and more uneven — than either side predicted.
articles.image_caption: The United States Capitol in Washington, D.C., where the One Big Beautiful Bill Act was passed
articles.nri_angle: Every H-1B holder, green card carrier, and naturalised citizen who sends money to family in India now operates under this law. The exemptions favour those who bank digitally; the tax bites hardest on cash-and-counter senders — a distinction that splits the diaspora along class lines.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian Banks Are Offering NRIs Up to Seven Per Cent on Dollar Deposits. The Window Closes in Eleven Weeks.
articles.excerpt: The RBI's special swap facility has removed the hedging cost that kept FCNR(B) rates stuck below four per cent. Indian Bank alone is targeting two billion dollars by September. Here is what NRIs need to know before the deadline.
articles.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India headquarters in Mumbai, which launched the special forex swap window for NRI deposits
articles.nri_angle: For NRIs parking idle dollars in US savings accounts yielding under one per cent, or even in Treasuries at four-and-a-half per cent, this is a rare moment when parking money in India carries no currency risk and pays meaningfully more — but only until September 30.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Tax Department Can Now See Your Foreign Bank Accounts. Here Is What Every NRI Needs to Know.
articles.excerpt: A CBDT order integrates overseas financial data from over a hundred countries into taxpayers' Annual Information Statements, closing one of the last gaps in cross-border tax visibility.
articles.image_caption: Aaykar Bhavan, the Income Tax Department's office in Pune, India
articles.nri_angle: NRIs with bank accounts, investments, or property in India now face unprecedented transparency — their overseas financial information from the US, UK, Canada, and other AEOI countries will appear in their Indian tax records, raising the compliance stakes for the 30-million-strong diaspora.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: One Indian Sailor Missing, Ten Rescued After Iran Strikes Container Ship in the Strait of Hormuz
articles.excerpt: The attack on the GFS Galaxy is the fourth time in three months that a vessel with Indian crew has been hit in the Hormuz standoff. India's 300,000-strong seafaring community is running out of safe passage.
articles.image_caption: Naval vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz, where Indian-crewed commercial ships have repeatedly been struck since April 2026
articles.nri_angle: Indian seafarers — over 300,000 strong — are disproportionately exposed to the Hormuz standoff. Four ships with Indian crews have been struck since April. Maritime families in coastal India and across the diaspora live with a unique anxiety each time a vessel is hit.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: From Tandoor to Michelin: Indian Fine Dining Is Conquering the World's Most Demanding Markets

articles.nri_angle: Indian-origin chefs and restaurateurs are leading the global expansion, reshaping perceptions of Indian cuisine and building cultural bridges through food.

articles.title: Sunil Bharti Mittal Calls Indian Diaspora a 'Beautiful Bridge' as USISPF Honours Him with Leadership Award
articles.excerpt: The Bharti Enterprises founder was honoured alongside RTX's Christopher Calio and Fairfax Financial's V. Prem Watsa at the IX USISPF Leadership Summit in Washington.
articles.image_caption: Sunil Bharti Mittal at the USISPF Leadership Summit
articles.nri_angle: Mittal's speech directly celebrated the five-million-strong Indian diaspora in the US as the connective tissue between the two nations, with trade deal implications for NRI business leaders.

articles.title: Five Thousand Visas, Working Holidays, and a Twenty-Billion-Dollar Promise. Inside the India–New Zealand FTA's Diaspora Dividend.
articles.excerpt: The landmark free-trade agreement signed in April and celebrated during Modi's Wellington visit this week contains the most NRI-friendly mobility provisions India has ever secured from a developed nation. A breakdown of what it means for professionals, students, and young Indians.
articles.image_caption: Prime Minister Narendra Modi with New Zealand Prime Minister Christopher Luxon. The two nations signed a landmark Free Trade Agreement in April 2026. (Photo: Government of India via Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: This FTA is the most NRI-friendly mobility framework India has secured from a developed nation. The 5,000 skilled-worker visa quota, uncapped student admissions with extended post-study work rights, and 1,000 working-holiday visas create a structured pathway for Indians to live, work, and study in New Zealand — directly benefiting the 350,000-strong Indian Kiwi community and millions of prospective migrants.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The American India Foundation Just Raised a Record $3.8 Million in One Night. Here Is Why It Matters.
articles.excerpt: At its twenty-fifth-anniversary gala inside Cipriani Wall Street, AIF honoured Infosys CEO Salil Parekh, retired TD Bank chief Bharat Masrani, and BNY — while setting a new fundraising benchmark for Indian diaspora philanthropy in the United States.
articles.image_caption: The American India Foundation raised a record .8 million at its 25th-anniversary gala in New York
articles.nri_angle: The AIF gala is one of the single largest diaspora fundraising events on the US calendar. Its record haul underscores the growing financial muscle and institutional maturity of Indian-American philanthropy — a community estimated to donate $3–5 billion annually. For NRIs debating where to direct their giving, the evening offers a case study in how scale, accountability, and marquee honourees can move the needle.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
